roadmap.goal: Slice 03 (US-04): Throughput PBC natural process limits over time. Ship the second snapshot family end to end — ProcessBehaviorSnapshot entity + repository + a REAL additive EF migration on all providers (03-01) -> ProcessBehaviorRecordingHandler on the SAME TeamDataRefreshed / PortfolioFeaturesRefreshed events the percentiles recorder already subscribes, with its own MetricFamily="ProcessBehavior" observability contract (03-02) -> IProcessBehaviorSeriesQuery + ProcessBehaviorSnapshotDto + process-behavior-over-time?type= GET on both MetricsControllers (03-03) -> demo backfill extended so demo/screenshot E2Es render populated NPL charts (03-04) -> a NEW "PBC Over Time" widget in Predictability with a metric-type toggle (Throughput active) rendering UNPL/Average/LNPL and the D6 honest empty state (03-05) -> Playwright POM + spec + full local quality-gate sweep (03-06). Closes milestone-3 Scenarios 10, 11 and 12 plus the ProcessBehaviorSnapshot half of milestone-1 Scenario 6.
roadmap.overview: Single phase (03), 6 steps in dependency order. Unlike slice-02 this slice is NOT a pure extension: it adds a second table, a second repository, a second recording handler, a second read port, a second DTO, two new controller actions and a whole new frontend widget. The pipeline SHAPE is reused (events, upsert-per-day idempotency, per-family failure containment, demo backfill idiom, empty-state contract); the code is new because the NPL triple Unpl/Average/Lnpl is a different shape from the four-percentile row (ADR-106). Backbone: schema first (03-01, the only step with DDL), then write path (03-02), then read path (03-03), then demo data (03-04), then UI (03-05), then E2E + gates (03-06). RED = RED-by-skip (project convention, DISTILL [REF] RED Mechanism): NUnit ATs / Playwright specs are authored with [Ignore("pending — DELIVER (epic-5427 slice-03)")] / test.skip alongside minimal type skeletons so main always compiles and stays green; each step un-ignores only its own scenarios and implements them to GREEN. EFFORT CAVEAT: the slice brief reference-classes this at <=1 day. This decomposition totals ~15h (~2 days) and the estimate is deliberately NOT cut to fit — slice-02 was briefed at <=0.5 day and actually took ~1.5 days, and slice-03 carries strictly more surface than slice-02 did (a real migration + a new widget from scratch, neither of which slice-02 had). Treat the brief's number as optimistic, not as a scope reduction.

steps.name: ProcessBehaviorSnapshot entity + ProcessBehaviorMetricType enum + repository + DbSet/unique index + REAL additive EF migration on all providers
criteria: New entity `ProcessBehaviorSnapshot : IEntity` with `Id`, `OwnerId`, `OwnerType`, `RecordedAt` (DateOnly), `MetricType` (of the NEW enum type), `Unpl`, `Average`, `Lnpl`. Value types match the source: `ProcessBehaviourChart.Average / UpperNaturalProcessLimit / LowerNaturalProcessLimit` are all `int`, so the columns are `int` — do NOT widen to double and invent precision the compute path does not have.

New enum `ProcessBehaviorMetricType` with `Throughput` FIRST and, this slice, ONLY `Throughput`. Carry the same XML-doc warning as `MetricType`: persisted as the integer ordinal, APPEND-only, never reorder or renumber. Slice 04 appends WorkItemAge / Wip / CycleTime / Arrivals / FeatureSize.

Do NOT reuse the existing `MetricType` enum for this table. `MetricType` means percentile family (CycleTime, WorkItemAge); the PBC set is a different, larger domain (six types incl. FeatureSize) and sharing the enum would couple two independently-growing ordinals to one another.

`IProcessBehaviorSnapshotRepository` + a thin `RepositoryBase<T>` implementation, byte-for-byte the same idiom as `IPercentilesOverTimeSnapshotRepository` / `PercentilesOverTimeSnapshotRepository` — no bespoke query methods beyond what the base gives.

`LighthouseAppContext` gains the `DbSet<ProcessBehaviorSnapshot>` plus a UNIQUE index on the natural key `(OwnerId, OwnerType, MetricType, RecordedAt)`. Note the key has FOUR parts, not five: there is no horizon dimension for NPLs, so no sentinel column and no NoHorizon constant is needed here.
`Program.cs` registers the repository in DI. The handler registration lands in 03-02, not here.

A REAL EF migration named `AddProcessBehaviorSnapshot` is generated for EVERY supported provider via the existing `CreateMigration` PowerShell script — never `dotnet ef migrations add` (CLAUDE.md). Verify both a Sqlite and a Postgres migration pair (.cs + .Designer.cs) appear, mirroring the slice-01 pair 20260724065010_AddPercentilesOverTimeSnapshot (Sqlite) / 20260724065020_AddPercentilesOverTimeSnapshot (Postgres).

The migration is ADDITIVE / EXPAND-ONLY: one CreateTable plus one CreateIndex, zero DropColumn / DropTable / AlterColumn on any existing table. A rollback of app code leaves an inert orphan table and loses no data.
Entity unit tests mirroring `PercentilesOverTimeSnapshotTests.cs`, and repository tests mirroring `PercentilesOverTimeSnapshotRepositoryTests.cs` (EF InMemory).

A Postgres-container migration test `ProcessBehaviorSnapshotMigrationTests.cs` mirroring `PercentilesOverTimeSnapshotMigrationTests.cs` asserts the table AND the unique index exist after migrating, and that inserting a duplicate natural key is rejected. Postgres is the provider that actually enforces the constraint — EF InMemory cannot see this, which is exactly why the container test is mandatory.
`dotnet build` zero warnings and `dotnet test` green at step end; only this step's entity/repository/migration tests are un-ignored.

steps.name: ProcessBehaviorRecordingHandler — daily Throughput NPL upsert on the existing refresh events, own observability family
criteria: New `ProcessBehaviorRecordingHandler : IDomainEventHandler<TeamDataRefreshed>, IDomainEventHandler<PortfolioFeaturesRefreshed>` — the SAME two events `PercentilesOverTimeRecordingHandler` and `BlockedCountSnapshotRecordingHandler` already subscribe. No new event, no new trigger, no scheduler.

A SECOND handler is correct here and does not violate the OUT-5427-pipeline-reuse KPI: that KPI requires one pipeline per metric FAMILY shape, and ADR-106 already split the NPL triple from the percentile row into two tables. What must be reused is the shape — events, upsert-per-day, failure containment, cache invalidation — not the class.

`private const string MetricFamily = "ProcessBehavior";` and its OWN message template, e.g. "Process behaviour snapshot recording failed for {OwnerType} {OwnerId} ({MetricFamily})". It does NOT share or reuse the percentiles handler's template. Logging the metric TYPE instead of the FAMILY was the adversarial-review BLOCKER in slice-02 (fixed in 724099f32) — do not reintroduce it.

Reads today's limits via `ITeamMetricsService.GetThroughputProcessBehaviourChart(team, startDate, endDate)` / `IPortfolioMetricsService.GetThroughputProcessBehaviourChart(portfolio, startDate, endDate)`. Zero PBC math is reimplemented.

HONESTY GATE (this is the sharpest correctness risk in the slice): `ProcessBehaviourChart.NotReady(...)` returns Average = UNPL = LNPL = 0. When `Status != BaselineStatus.Ready` the handler MUST NOT write a row. Recording zeros would render three flat lines pinned at zero — a fabricated process, and a direct violation of D6 empty-state honesty. A unit test drives each non-Ready BaselineStatus (BaselineMissing, BaselineInvalid, InsufficientData) and asserts zero rows written.

Idempotent per day: upsert on the natural-key predicate `(OwnerId, OwnerType, MetricType, RecordedAt = today)`; a same-day re-refresh updates in place. A test drives two consecutive refreshes and asserts exactly one row (US-02 AC2 semantics, now for the NPL family).

Per-metric-type failure containment mirroring `RecordFamily`: the Throughput read is wrapped so that when slice 04 appends five more types, one failing type cannot discard rows another type already staged. Build the loop-with-inner-try seam NOW even though only one type is active — retrofitting it later means re-touching a shipped handler.

Own `try/catch` at the top level plus the structured Error log; the caller's single `Save()` persists whatever was staged. Do NOT add a log-and-rethrow wrapper (Sonar S2139) — the Epic 5121 dispatcher swallows handler errors by design and the handler owns its own observability.

Read-cache invalidation in a `finally`, exactly as the percentiles handler does, and test-pinned on BOTH the success and the exception path. The slice-01 omission of this guard broke an unrelated @premium E2E; it is a standing regression rule.
A forced-exception test asserts the refresh path stays green (US-02 AC4 / DDD-6) and that the recording-failed event carries MetricFamily = "ProcessBehavior".
`Program.cs` registers the handler for both event types alongside the existing recording handlers.

OPEN QUESTION TO RESOLVE AND RECORD IN THIS STEP (DESIGN "PBC-over-time day grain"): decide and justify the lookback window passed to GetThroughputProcessBehaviourChart for an as-of-today snapshot, and confirm the per-refresh recompute is cheap enough. Match whatever window the point-in-time throughputPbc widget uses so the recorded limits equal what the user sees today — read that call site before choosing. If the recompute turns out to be hot, cache rather than changing the grain. Write the decision into the step's commit message and carry it to the ADR-106/107 amendment at finalization.
`dotnet build` zero warnings, `dotnet test` green; only this step's handler tests are un-ignored.

steps.name: Demo backfill — backdate Throughput NPL rows for demo owners, per-family idempotency guard extended
criteria: DECISION: EXTEND the existing `DemoPercentilesBackfillHandler` rather than adding a second demo handler. Justification: identical trigger, identical IsDemo gate, identical 14-day window and identical idempotency mechanism; a second handler would duplicate the demo-gate and window logic and risk the two charts on one screenshot disagreeing about their date range. This is also the reuse-analysis default (EXTEND unless the computation genuinely differs) and stays inside ADR-109's decision — the ADR names the handler as the epic's demo-backdating seam, not as a percentiles-only class. Update its XML doc to say it backdates BOTH over-time families; do not rename the class (churn across a shipped registration for no behavioural gain).

Injects `IProcessBehaviorSnapshotRepository` alongside the percentiles repository and backdates Throughput NPL rows over the SAME 14-day window the percentile backfill uses, so both widgets show an identically-dated range in demo screenshots.

The idempotency guard is extended to cover the ProcessBehavior family per the slice-02 rule: the guard is PER METRIC FAMILY, never per owner. An owner-scoped guard would make every newly-added family a permanent no-op on environments already backfilled for percentiles — exactly the bug slice-02 fixed. A regression test asserts an owner already CT+WIA-backfilled still gains Throughput NPL rows.

Demo-gated only (IsDemo=true connections). Real tenants stay forward-only and see the honest empty state until days accrue — backfilling real tenants would fabricate never-measured history (D5, ADR-109).

Backdated NPL values must be plausible and internally consistent: LNPL <= Average <= UNPL for every generated day. A degenerate or inverted triple would render a visibly broken chart in the docs screenshots.
The handler's failure isolation and demo gate remain intact; adding a family must not change behaviour for owners that have no PBC data.
`dotnet build` zero warnings, `dotnet test` green; un-ignore only this step's demo-backfill tests.
